question: When does Lent take place?
explanation: The 40 days before Easter are known as Lent. It is a time when Christians take time to reflect and prepare for Easter.

question: Which of the following national galleries is NOT located in London?
explanation: The National Museum is located in Cardiff, Wales.

question: How much can you be fined if you watch TV but do not have a TV licence?
explanation: You will receive a fine up to £1,000 if you watch TV but do not have a TV licence.

question: How old is the clock at the house of the parliament in London, also known as ‘Big Ben’?
explanation: Big Ben is the nickname for the great bell of the clock at the House of Parliament in London. The clock is over 150 years old and is a popular tourist attraction.

question: Which is the oldest tennis tournament in the world?
explanation: The most famous tournament hosted in Britain is The Wimbledon Championships, which takes place each year at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club. It is the oldest tennis tournament in the world and the only ‘Grand Slam’ event played on grass.

question: Where is the ‘Eden Project’ located?
explanation: The Eden Project is located in Cornwall, in the south west of England.

question: Which of the following is a traditional food from Northern Ireland?
explanation: Ulster fry – a fried meal with bacon, eggs, sausage, black pudding, tomatoes, mushrooms, soda bread and potato bread – is a traditional Northern Ireland.

question: Who is the author of the murder mystery play ‘The Mousetrap’?
explanation: The Mousetrap, a murder-mystery play by Dame Agatha Christie, has been running in the west end since 1952 and has had the longest initial run of any show in history.

question: When is April Fool’s Day?
explanation: April Fool’s Day is on the 1st of April.

question: Where is the city of Bradford located?
explanation: Bradford is located in England.

question: Which flag comprises a red cross on a white ground?
options: The cross of St Andrew, patron saint of Scotland
The cross of St David, patron saint of Wales
The cross of St Patrick, patron saint of Ireland
The cross of St George, patron saint of England
correctAnswers: The cross of St George, patron saint of England
explanation: The cross of St George, patron saint of England, is a red cross on a white ground.

question: What is celebrated during Diwali?
options: Jesus Christ rising from the dead
The victory of good over evil and the gaining of knowledge
The founding of the Sikh community known as the Khalsa
The beginning of the winter season
correctAnswers: The victory of good over evil and the gaining of knowledge
explanation: Diwalli celebrates the victory of good over evil and the gaining of knowledge.

question: According to the 2011 Census, what percentage of the population identified themselves as Christian?
explanation: In the 2011 census, 59% of people identified themselves as Christians.

question: Which golf ‘Major’ tournament is hosted by a different golf course every year?
explanation: The Open Championship is the only ‘Major’ tournament held outside United States. It is hosted by a different golf course every year.

question: Which British actor has recently won an Oscar?
explanation: Recent British actors to have won Oscars include Colin Firth, Sir Antony Hopkins, Dame Judi Dench, Kate Winslet and Tilda Swinton.

question: What TWO names are given to the day before Lent?
explanation: The day before Lent starts is called Shrove Tuesday, or Pancake Day.

question: Which of the following landmarks is the largest expanse of fresh water in mainland Britain?
explanation: Loch Lomond is the largest expanse of fresh water in mainland Britain and probably the best-known part of the park.

question: Who wrote the music for the popular show Jesus Christ Superstar?
options: Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice
Hans Holbein and Sir Anthony Van Dyck
correctAnswers: Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice
explanation: Andrew Lloyd Webber has written the music for shows which have been popular throughout the world, including, in collaboration with Tim Rice, Jesus Christ Superstar and Evita, and also Cats and The Phantom of the Opera.

question: Pantomimes are a British tradition that many theatres produce during:
explanation: Many theatres produce a pantomime at Christmas time.

question: Which of the following meals is made of bacon, eggs, sausage, black pudding, tomatoes, mushrooms, soda bread and potato bread?
explanation: Ulster fry is a fried meal from Northern Ireland with bacon, eggs, sausage, black pudding, tomatoes, mushrooms, soda bread and potato bread.

question: Which of the following is a showcase of mainly theatre and comedy performances?
explanation: The Fringe is a showcase of mainly theatre and comedy performances.

question: Which of the following are public holidays in Scotland (choose TWO options)?
explanation: In Scotland, the 1st of January and the 2nd of January are bank holidays.

question: What name is given to the period of time when Christians take time to reflect and prepare for Easter?
explanation: Lent is a time when Christians take time to reflect and prepare for Easter.

question: In Wales, many people speak Gaelic – a completely different language from English – and it is taught in schools and universities:
explanation: False.﻿In Wales, many people speak Welsh – a completely different language from English – and it is taught in schools and universities.
